head: claude/claude-md-reference-split
title: docs: split the API payload reference out of CLAUDE.md (-34.4%, verbatim)
body:
Splits the **API payload reference** out of `CLAUDE.md` into `docs/reference/bot-api-reference.md`, **verbatim**. Slice 1 of the boot-read reduction dispatched by the manager (MI-41 item B).

## Why

`CLAUDE.md` is **the only surface that reaches a session before it acts** — project hooks do not run on Claude Code on the web (verified 2026-08-26) and CI guards fire at merge, which is after the wrong work is already built. So what it costs to read is a real constraint on every session. The moved sections are *lookup* material: they answer "what does this endpoint return", a question a session has only once it is already in the code.

## Measured

Population: `CLAUDE.md` at `origin/main` `d8aac5c6`, byte counts from `wc -c`, section boundaries at `^#{1,3} ` headings.

| | bytes |
|---|--:|
| `CLAUDE.md` before | 430,453 |
| moved verbatim | 154,074 |
| index added back | 4,062 |
| **`CLAUDE.md` after** | **282,656** (**−34.4%**) |

⚠️ **This is NOT the boot-read problem solved, and the PR body says so deliberately.** The five-file boot read goes 1,538,532 → 1,389,008 B — **only −9.7%** — because `ROADMAP.md` (648,407 B) is **42%** of that set and is untouched. Filed as `BL-20260902-BOOT-READ-IS-427K-TOKENS-AND-ROADMAP-IS-42-PERCENT-OF-IT` so nobody quotes the −34.4% against the wrong denominator.

## What moved, and what deliberately did not

**Moved** (`## Dashboard REST API (S-014)` route table, `BotStats` / `Position` shapes, `## CORS`, the `## Diagnostic API (S-051)` route table) — **verbatim, warnings attached**. Most of those ⚠️ blocks exist because an earlier version of the same row was stale *in the dangerous direction*; separating a row from its correction would be worse than leaving both.

**Verified programmatically, not by reading**: both blocks are byte-identical to their originals; the prose either side is byte-identical; the generated SESSION-BRIEF block is unchanged. The whole `CLAUDE.md` diff is 67 added / 261 removed lines and every changed line is accounted for.

**Kept in `CLAUDE.md`** because they bind *before* you open anything: CORS is load-bearing for the only live consumer; a new route needs a row in `docs/api-tier-policy.md` or `api-tier-policy-guard` fails CI; the diag surface's 503-vs-401 contract and its **read-only premise**, which the closed token-rotation decision rests on.

**NOT moved, and named so nobody assumes coverage:** `## Environment Variables` (131,620 B), `## PM-side session capabilities` (22,470 B — argued to *stay*, it is the densest boot-binding content in the file), `## Important Notes` (17,823 B). Proposal with resolution criteria: `docs/design/boot-read-size-PROPOSAL.md`.

## Governance was re-pointed, not dropped

`docs/reference/bot-api-reference.md` is registered in `ACTIVE_DOCS` in `check_canonical_doc_coherence.py`. **Not optional:** the `POST /api/bot/prop/report` fail-CLOSED value contract reads text that lives in the moved table, so omitting it would have **retired a live check by moving the text it reads**. **Verified by positive control** — planting the stale `"token-gated … when set"` phrasing in the new file makes the guard FAIL; reverting makes it pass.

Hierarchy mirrors updated in both `CLAUDE.md` and `CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md` (the `canonical-doc-coherence` mirror check still matches — it normalises to keys), plus `docs/api-tier-policy.md`'s cross-reference and `docs/claude/INDEX.md`.

## Two pre-existing guard defects the move surfaced, both fixed with tests

1. **`check_backlog_refs` was blind to a file SPLIT.** It exempts an id "already cited in **this file** at base", so a verbatim move into a *new* file defeated it and five long-standing dangling ids read as newly introduced — all five already attributed to `BL-20260730-CITED-BUT-UNFILED-BACKLOG-IDS`. Now falls back to *cited anywhere in the tree at base* for a path absent at base; an id cited nowhere at base still fails.
2. **Every `FU-` citation dangled by construction.** `REF` matches `BL`/`MB`/`FU` while `filed_ids` read only `docs/claude/*backlog*.json`; `FU-` rows live in `comms/follow_ups.json`. **Measured**: of 13 `FU-` ids cited across the guard's `SEARCH_DIRS`, **12 are genuinely filed** and now resolve; the thirteenth is cited and never filed and still dangles — it is the live positive control. **More accurate, not quieter.**

⚠️ **The split test is a real instrument, and its first version was not.** It deleted the source file, which git rendered as a pure rename emitting no `+` lines at all — so it passed with the fix **disabled** and proved nothing. Caught by running the negative control, not by reading the test. It now keeps the source file and asserts the diff actually carries an added line citing the id before asserting anything about the verdict.

## Verification

- **`scripts/ci/run_guards.py --base main`: PASS 50 · FAIL 0 · SKIP 20.**
- `tests/test_check_backlog_refs.py`: 23 passed (14 pre-existing + 9 new).
- The two guard fixes each pinned by a **negative control** run in-session: disabling the fix makes the new test fail, restoring it makes it pass.
- `pytest` and `import-linter` were absent from the container and were installed so these could actually be run rather than reported unverified.

## ⚠️ Coordination — one file is contested

`CLAUDE.md`'s generated **SESSION-BRIEF** block is owned by the manager session (`session_011JWFxuYAaEQKCFCmG6gnHJ`, declared 05:48Z). My `OPEN-ITEMS.json` row changed the registers, so `session-brief-guard` **required** a re-render; that diff is **4 insertions / 1 deletion** (my row plus the count) and is row-wise resolvable against anything the manager renders. All my other `CLAUDE.md` edits are below line 962; the brief lives at 91–152.

`docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json` was edited by **text splice, not re-serialisation** — the diff is `21 added / 0 removed`. An earlier attempt via `json.dumps` reformatted 643 lines and was reverted.

## Scope

Tier 1 throughout — docs, two CI guards, tests. Nothing touches `src/`, `config/`, an order path, risk caps, or a VM.

**Left as a DRAFT. The manager owns the merge.**
